title: Finals Exam Reviewer
description: Modules 10–14: Code Reuse and Class Hierarchy, Interfaces, Abstract Class and Interface, Polymorphism, and Modularity. Multiple choice + output tracing.

questions.question: By allowing information of a superclass to be taken on by subclasses, the information is said to be:
options: Duplicated in every object
Hidden from the subclass
Deleted from the superclass
Reused at the subclass level
questions.explanation: Module 10 - Code Reuse, Making Changes in Class Hierarchy

questions.question: Which statement describes changes to software specification?
options: Changes affect only the user interface
Changes are only allowed before coding
Changes to software specification are inevitable
Changes to software specification never happen
questions.explanation: Module 10 - Code Reuse, Making Changes in Class Hierarchy

questions.question: Which of the following is one of the situations discussed for changes in a class hierarchy?
options: Change in the operating system for some subclasses
Change in property definition for some subclasses
Change in the programming language for all subclasses
Change in the compiler used by the superclass
questions.explanation: Module 10 - Code Reuse, Making Changes in Class Hierarchy. The three situations: change for all subclasses, change for some subclasses, and adding/deleting a class.

questions.question: Without inheritance, a change to an attribute shared by several classes must be made:
options: Individually in every class, which may lead to inconsistency
Automatically by the compiler for every class that uses it
Only in main(), since attributes are defined there for all classes
Only once, in the superclass, and it propagates to every subclass
questions.explanation: Module 10 - Code Reuse, Making Changes in Class Hierarchy

questions.question: With inheritance, a change to an attribute defined in the superclass is:
options: Made in the last subclass and passed up to the superclass
Copied by hand into each subclass of the hierarchy
Limited to the superclass, and it propagates to the subclasses
Made in main() and passed to every class
questions.explanation: Module 10 - Code Reuse, Making Changes in Class Hierarchy

questions.question: Defining a property once in the superclass and letting subclasses inherit it results in:
options: Uniform and consistent property definitions and minimal redundancy
Different property definitions and more redundancy in each subclass
Inconsistent definitions that must be repeated at the subclass level
Harder maintenance, since every subclass must be changed separately
questions.explanation: Module 10 - Code Reuse, Making Changes in Class Hierarchy

questions.question: A redefining method has the same method name and parameter definition as the redefined method, but:
options: It cannot return a value
It must have a different name
It must have more parameters
Its implementation may differ
questions.explanation: Module 10 - Code Reuse, Making Changes in Class Hierarchy

questions.question: When adding a new class into an existing class hierarchy, it is always recommended that the new class be created as a:
options: Copy of an existing class
Subclass in the class hierarchy
Superclass of all existing classes
Separate program
questions.explanation: Module 10 - Code Reuse, Making Changes in Class Hierarchy

questions.question: Subclassing is a desired design practice in object-oriented software engineering because:
options: It has minimal impact on software maintenance
It makes every attribute public
It prevents code reuse
It removes the need for constructors in subclasses
questions.explanation: Module 10 - Code Reuse, Making Changes in Class Hierarchy. Subclassing is specialization.

questions.question: Deleting subclasses that are NOT superclasses to other classes:
options: Requires rewriting the superclass
Breaks every other class in the class hierarchy
Is not allowed in Java
Has a minimal impact on software maintenance
questions.explanation: Module 10 - Code Reuse, Making Changes in Class Hierarchy

questions.question: What is code reuse in a class hierarchy?
options: Every subclass rewrites all of the methods of its superclass again
Methods are called again and again inside a loop until it ends
Subclasses use members already defined in a superclass
Objects copy all of their data into brand new objects when created
questions.explanation: Module 10 - Code Reuse, Making Changes in Class Hierarchy

questions.question: What is a superclass?
options: A class that contains only static methods
A general class whose members are inherited by subclasses
A class that inherits all members from a more general class
A class that cannot have any subclasses at all
questions.explanation: Module 10 - Code Reuse, Making Changes in Class Hierarchy

questions.question: What is a subclass?
options: A class with no attributes or methods
A specialized class that inherits from another class
A general class that many other classes inherit from
A class that cannot inherit from any class
questions.explanation: Module 10 - Code Reuse, Making Changes in Class Hierarchy

questions.question: What does it mean to redefine (override) a method?
options: A method is deleted from the superclass
A class defines two methods with the same name but different parameters
A subclass gives a same-signature method its own body
A method is copied into every subclass unchanged
questions.explanation: Module 10 - Code Reuse, Making Changes in Class Hierarchy

questions.question: Trace the output (Default constructors in a chain): what does this program print?

questions.explanation: Module 10 - Code Reuse, Making Changes in Class Hierarchy. Based on the OOP Quiz (Set A). Nothing was set, so the inherited fields keep the defaults from Person() and Employee(). Professor's course() appends "," + research.

questions.question: Trace the output (Setters and an overloaded constructor): what does this program print?
questions.instruction: Type each printed line on its own line, in order.
questions.explanation: Module 10 - Code Reuse, Making Changes in Class Hierarchy. Based on the OOP Quiz (Set A). The setters are inherited from Person and Employee; Professor(String) stores "Thesis1" as the course.

questions.question: Trace the output (A getter that changes its own field): what does this program print?
questions.instruction: Type each printed line on its own line, in order.
questions.explanation: Module 10 - Code Reuse, Making Changes in Class Hierarchy. Based on the OOP Quiz (Set A). course() saves the longer string back into the field, so calling it a second time appends research again.

questions.question: Trace the output (Same method name, different classes): what does this program print?
questions.instruction: Type each printed line on its own line, in order.
questions.explanation: Module 10 - Code Reuse, Making Changes in Class Hierarchy. Based on the OOP Quiz (Set A). Lecturer redefines course() to return its own field; values that were never set keep the defaults.

questions.question: Trace the output (Redefining pay() with super): what does this program print?
questions.instruction: Type each printed line on its own line, in order.
questions.explanation: Module 10 - Code Reuse, Making Changes in Class Hierarchy. Manager redefines pay() and still reuses Employee's version through super.pay(); Clerk inherits pay() unchanged.

questions.question: The capability to inherit from more than one class is called:
options: Single inheritance
Encapsulation
Polymorphism
Multiple inheritance
questions.explanation: Module 11 - Concepts of Interface, Inheritance Using Interface

questions.question: Which of the following languages allows a subclass to inherit from more than one parent class?
options: Neither C++ nor Java
Java
Both C++ and Java
questions.explanation: Module 11 - Concepts of Interface, Inheritance Using Interface

questions.question: Why is multiple inheritance prohibited in Java?
options: Java does not support classes with parents, so only interfaces can be inherited by a subclass
Interfaces are slower than classes, so Java limits each class to one parent
Parent classes may have identical names, and super() would be unclear with multiple parents
Constructors are not allowed in Java subclasses, so super() cannot be called
questions.explanation: Module 11 - Concepts of Interface, Inheritance Using Interface

questions.question: A class inheriting from a superclass that has inherited from another superclass represents:
options: Multiple inheritance through an interface
Single inheritance with multiple generations
An anonymous inner class with two parents
Multiple inheritance with a single generation
questions.explanation: Module 11 - Concepts of Interface, Inheritance Using Interface

questions.question: Java's alternative to multiple inheritance is the:
options: Interface
Package
Abstract method
Static variable
questions.explanation: Module 11 - Concepts of Interface, Inheritance Using Interface

questions.question: In an interface, all methods (if any) are implicitly:
options: public and static
private and static
protected and final
public and abstract
questions.explanation: Module 11 - Concepts of Interface, Inheritance Using Interface

questions.question: In an interface, all data items (if any) are implicitly:
options: protected and static
public and abstract
public, static, and final
private and abstract
questions.explanation: Module 11 - Concepts of Interface, Inheritance Using Interface

questions.question: An interface is a description of:
options: The private data of a class
What a class does, but not how it is done
The constructor of a class
How a class does something, but not what it does
questions.explanation: Module 11 - Concepts of Interface, Inheritance Using Interface

questions.question: Which keyword is placed in a class header to use an interface?
options: implements
super
interface
extends
questions.explanation: Module 11 - Concepts of Interface, Inheritance Using Interface

questions.question: Whereas extends lets a subclass use nonprivate, nonoverridden members of its parent, implements requires the class to:
options: Inherit the parent's private data and methods
Become an interface
Call super() twice
Implement its own version of each method
questions.explanation: Module 11 - Concepts of Interface, Inheritance Using Interface

questions.question: The interface construct in Java is used with single inheritance to provide:
options: Some form of static binding
Some form of operation overloading
Some form of information hiding
Some form of multiple inheritance
questions.explanation: Module 11 - Concepts of Interface, Inheritance Using Interface

questions.question: When a class implements an interface but does not implement all of its methods:
options: The class must be declared abstract
The interface methods are ignored when the program runs
The compiler adds empty bodies for the missing methods automatically
The class becomes final and can no longer be extended
questions.explanation: Module 11 - Concepts of Interface, Inheritance Using Interface

questions.question: A class Dog2 extends Dog and implements Worker. Which statement is true?
options: A Dog2 is a Dog, but it is not a Worker
A Dog2 is neither a Dog nor a Worker
A Dog2 "is a" Dog and "is a" Worker
A Dog2 is a Worker, but it is not a Dog
questions.explanation: Module 11 - Concepts of Interface, Inheritance Using Interface. A class that implements an interface represents a situation similar to inheritance.

questions.question: What is an interface in Java?
options: A named collection of related classes
A construct of abstract methods that a class must implement
A class from which objects can be instantiated
A class intended to be extended, not directly instantiated
questions.explanation: Module 11 - Concepts of Interface, Inheritance Using Interface

questions.question: What is multiple inheritance?
options: Inheriting from more than one class
Having many objects of one class
Inheriting from one class only
Having several methods with one name
questions.explanation: Module 11 - Concepts of Interface, Inheritance Using Interface

questions.question: Which keyword is used for a class to inherit from a superclass?
options: inherits
super
implements
extends
questions.explanation: Module 11 - Concepts of Interface, Inheritance Using Interface

questions.question: How many interfaces can a Java class implement?
options: Only one interface
None, if it extends a class
Any number of interfaces
At most two interfaces
questions.explanation: Module 11 - Concepts of Interface, Inheritance Using Interface

questions.question: What is the output of this program?
options: I am a dog who works / Woof!
Woof! / Woof! / I am a dog who works
The program does not compile, because Dog does not implement Worker
Woof! / I am a dog who works
questions.explanation: Module 11 - Concepts of Interface, Inheritance Using Interface. Output: Woof! / Woof! / I am a dog who works. work() calls the inherited speak() first, so Woof! appears twice.

questions.question: Trace the output (Extends and implements): what does this program print?
questions.instruction: Type each printed line on its own line, in order.
questions.explanation: Module 11 - Concepts of Interface, Inheritance Using Interface. name() comes from Person through extends; tax() had to be written because of implements. RATE is an interface constant (public, static, final).

questions.question: Trace the output (Two interfaces in one class): what does this program print?
questions.instruction: Type each printed line on its own line, in order.
questions.explanation: Module 11 - Concepts of Interface, Inheritance Using Interface. A class can implement any number of interfaces, and its object can be referred to by either interface type.

questions.question: What happens when code tries to create an object of an abstract class with new?
options: The program runs but throws an error later
The object is created with default values
The object is created as an interface instead
The program does not compile
questions.explanation: Module 12 - Attributes and Methods in an Interface, Abstract Class and Interface. No objects of an abstract class can exist.

questions.question: You create an abstract class such as Animal only so that you can:
options: Instantiate it
Use it as a package
Extend it
Hide it from subclasses
questions.explanation: Module 12 - Attributes and Methods in an Interface, Abstract Class and Interface

questions.question: The @Override annotation for a method such as speak() is:
options: Not necessary, but it provides error checking and documentation
Used only in interfaces, never in subclasses
Used to create a new object of the parent class
Required, or the program will not compile at all without it
questions.explanation: Module 12 - Attributes and Methods in an Interface, Abstract Class and Interface

questions.question: Using the same method name to indicate different implementations is called:
options: Static binding
Polymorphism
Encapsulation
Bundling
questions.explanation: Module 12 - Attributes and Methods in an Interface, Abstract Class and Interface

questions.question: Data attributes declared in an interface construct are always:
options: static and final
protected and static
public and non-final
private and abstract
questions.explanation: Module 12 - Attributes and Methods in an Interface, Abstract Class and Interface. Static because there is only one copy; final because they are not modifiable.

questions.question: Names for values with a specific meaning that are declared in an interface, such as int RED = 1, are called:
options: Literals
Constants
Parameters
Variables
questions.explanation: Module 12 - Attributes and Methods in an Interface, Abstract Class and Interface

questions.question: All methods in an interface are:
options: Private methods hidden from every class that uses the interface
Static methods that the implementing class may not override
Abstract methods that any class using the interface must implement
Constructors that run when a class implements the interface
questions.explanation: Module 12 - Attributes and Methods in an Interface, Abstract Class and Interface

questions.question: Methods in an interface may NOT be static because:
options: Interfaces cannot contain methods, only constant data attributes
Static methods must have constructors, which interfaces do not have
Static methods are always private, so no class could call them
Static methods, being class specific, are never abstract
questions.explanation: Module 12 - Attributes and Methods in an Interface, Abstract Class and Interface

questions.question: Abstract classes and interfaces are similar in that:
options: A class can extend any number of either of them
You cannot instantiate concrete objects from either one
Both must have constructors that create objects
Both can contain only private methods and private data fields
questions.explanation: Module 12 - Attributes and Methods in an Interface, Abstract Class and Interface

questions.question: Abstract classes differ from interfaces because:
options: Interfaces can contain constructors and nonabstract methods, but abstract classes cannot
Interfaces can be instantiated with new, but abstract classes can never be instantiated
Abstract classes cannot have variables, but interfaces can have any kind of variable
Abstract classes can contain nonabstract methods, but all interface methods must be abstract
questions.explanation: Module 12 - Attributes and Methods in an Interface, Abstract Class and Interface

questions.question: A class can inherit from how many abstract superclasses, and implement how many interfaces?
options: Only one of each
None of either
Only one abstract superclass, but any number of interfaces
Any number of abstract superclasses, but only one interface
questions.explanation: Module 12 - Attributes and Methods in an Interface, Abstract Class and Interface

questions.question: Which is true about constructors in abstract classes and interfaces?
options: An interface has none; an abstract class's runs when a child object is created
Both have constructors that are called directly with the new operator
Neither can have a constructor, so subclasses must define all of them
An abstract class has no constructor; an interface's constructor is invoked when a class implements it
questions.explanation: Module 12 - Attributes and Methods in an Interface, Abstract Class and Interface

questions.question: Which is true about variables in interfaces and abstract classes?
options: Abstract class variables must be public, static, and final; interfaces have no restrictions on variables
Interface variables must be public, static, and final; abstract classes have no restrictions on variables
Neither may contain any variables at all
Both may only contain private variables
questions.explanation: Module 12 - Attributes and Methods in an Interface, Abstract Class and Interface

questions.question: An interface is generally used for achieving:
options: Multiple inheritance in Java
Information hiding in packages
Faster compilation
Static binding
questions.explanation: Module 12 - Attributes and Methods in an Interface, Abstract Class and Interface

questions.question: Given public abstract class LandVehicle { ... }, which statement is invalid?
options: class Car extends LandVehicle { }
LandVehicle l;
LandVehicle[] list = new LandVehicle[3];
LandVehicle l = new LandVehicle();
questions.explanation: Module 12 - Attributes and Methods in an Interface, Abstract Class and Interface

questions.question: Interface data fields must not be private because:
options: Private data cannot be static, and every field of an interface must be a static field
Private data uses too much memory, since every object would store its own copy of it
Interface methods cannot contain method bodies, so there is no way to retrieve private data
Interfaces are always final, so private fields would be hidden from the interface itself
questions.explanation: Module 12 - Attributes and Methods in an Interface, Abstract Class and Interface

questions.question: The purpose of creating an interface containing constants is to:
options: Create objects of the interface so that each object holds its own separate copy of the values
Provide a set of data that a number of classes can use without having to redeclare the values
Hide the data from every class so that the values can never be read by any program
Replace all the classes in a program with one interface that contains every method
questions.explanation: Module 12 - Attributes and Methods in an Interface, Abstract Class and Interface

questions.question: A class that has no name and is defined inside another class is a(n):
options: Interface
Abstract class
Package
Anonymous inner class
questions.explanation: Module 12 - Attributes and Methods in an Interface, Abstract Class and Interface

questions.question: When defining an anonymous inner class, you:
options: Use the new operator and do not use the keywords extends or implements
Must give the class a name and save it in its own separate .java file
Use the keyword implements, and declare the class outside the main class
Must use the keyword extends, and give the class a name before using it
questions.explanation: Module 12 - Attributes and Methods in an Interface, Abstract Class and Interface

questions.question: An anonymous inner class must either implement an interface or extend another class, and it must:
options: Have at least two constructors that call the superclass default constructor
Be declared static so that it can be instantiated more than once in the program
Override all the abstract methods in the interface or superclass
Be declared in a separate package from the class in which it is defined
questions.explanation: Module 12 - Attributes and Methods in an Interface, Abstract Class and Interface

questions.question: A variable whose value is assigned only once, which an anonymous inner class may access, is called:
options: Protected and static
Static
Abstract
Effectively final
questions.explanation: Module 12 - Attributes and Methods in an Interface, Abstract Class and Interface

questions.question: What is an abstract class?
options: A class containing only static methods and fields
A class that cannot have constructors of its own
A class intended to be extended, not directly instantiated
A class with no inherited properties or methods
questions.explanation: Module 12 - Attributes and Methods in an Interface, Abstract Class and Interface

questions.question: What is a concrete class?
options: A class from which objects can be instantiated
A class that declares only abstract methods
A class that can only be extended
A class that exists only as a diagram
questions.explanation: Module 12 - Attributes and Methods in an Interface, Abstract Class and Interface

questions.question: What is an abstract method?
options: A static method that belongs to the class and not the object
A method declared without a body that subclasses must implement
A method that can only be called once by the main method
A method that has a body but no return type or parameters
questions.explanation: Module 12 - Attributes and Methods in an Interface, Abstract Class and Interface

questions.question: Which keyword declares a class or method as abstract?
options: interface
static
abstract
final
questions.explanation: Module 12 - Attributes and Methods in an Interface, Abstract Class and Interface

questions.question: What is an anonymous inner class?
options: A public class that is saved alone in its own file
A class with no name that is defined inside another class
A class with a fixed name that cannot ever be changed
A class that has no methods and no attributes at all
questions.explanation: Module 12 - Attributes and Methods in an Interface, Abstract Class and Interface

questions.question: What is the output of this program?
options: GREENBLUE
The program does not compile, because RED, GREEN, and BLUE are not declared static
questions.explanation: Module 12 - Attributes and Methods in an Interface, Abstract Class and Interface. Output: 5. Interface data attributes are implicitly public, static, and final.

questions.question: Trace the output (Abstract class with a concrete method): what does this program print?
questions.instruction: Type each printed line on its own line, in order.
questions.explanation: Module 12 - Attributes and Methods in an Interface, Abstract Class and Interface. Vehicle cannot be instantiated, but its constructor runs through super() and its concrete info() calls the subclass's wheels().

questions.question: Trace the output (Implementing an abstract method differently): what does this program print?
questions.instruction: Type each printed line on its own line, in order.
questions.explanation: Module 12 - Attributes and Methods in an Interface, Abstract Class and Interface. Each concrete subclass must implement the abstract method; the overloaded constructors set different values.

questions.question: The binding of variables to operations at compile time is known as:
options: Static binding
Run-time binding
Dynamic binding
Late binding
questions.explanation: Module 13 - Polymorphism

questions.question: The binding of variables to operations at run time is known as:
options: Compile-time binding
Static binding
Dynamic binding
Early binding
questions.explanation: Module 13 - Polymorphism

questions.question: Which statement about static and dynamic binding is correct?
options: Static binding is limited and may lead to maintenance difficulty; dynamic binding provides design flexibility
Only procedural languages use dynamic binding
Both are identical
Static binding provides design flexibility; dynamic binding is limited and causes maintenance difficulty
questions.explanation: Module 13 - Polymorphism

questions.question: With static binding, adding a new kind of object to a program usually requires changes in:
options: Only the new class, with no other changes
No places, since the compiler adapts automatically
Only the main() method of the program
Multiple places in the code, which is error prone
questions.explanation: Module 13 - Polymorphism

questions.question: With dynamic binding, the method that runs for an overridden call is selected based on:
options: The order the classes were written in the file
The class of the object referenced at run time
The name of the variable that holds the reference
The type of the reference variable at compile time
questions.explanation: Module 13 - Polymorphism

questions.question: SalariedEmployee is a subclass of Employee. Which statement is true?
options: Every SalariedEmployee is an Employee, but not every Employee is a SalariedEmployee
Employee and SalariedEmployee are unrelated types that share no members
Every Employee is a SalariedEmployee, but not every SalariedEmployee is an Employee
No SalariedEmployee can ever be treated or stored as an Employee reference
questions.explanation: Module 13 - Polymorphism

questions.question: A reference is not an object, but it:
options: Is always abstract
Is created with the keyword new
Contains all the object's methods
Points to a memory address
questions.explanation: Module 13 - Polymorphism

questions.question: Assigning a variable or constant of one type to a variable of another type is called:
options: Static binding, early binding, or fixed binding
Promotion, implicit conversion, or upcasting
Encapsulation, bundling, or information hiding
Overloading, overriding, or redefining
questions.explanation: Module 13 - Polymorphism

questions.question: Using a reference polymorphically allows you to:
options: Make all methods static so that they are bound when the program is compiled
Create objects of an abstract class directly by using the keyword new
Extend a base class and use extended objects when a base class type is expected
Avoid writing subclasses, since one reference can hold every method
questions.explanation: Module 13 - Polymorphism

questions.question: In Java, all instance method calls are virtual method calls by default. This means:
options: The method used is determined when the program runs
The method is chosen by the compiler before the program runs
Methods must be static
Methods cannot be overridden
questions.explanation: Module 13 - Polymorphism

questions.question: An application's ability to select the correct subclass method depending on the argument type is known as:
options: Information hiding
Operation overloading
Static method binding
Dynamic method binding
questions.explanation: Module 13 - Polymorphism. It is also called late method binding.

questions.question: In Java, which methods use dynamic binding and which use static binding?
options: All methods use static binding
Instance methods use dynamic binding; class methods use static binding
Class methods use dynamic binding; instance methods use static binding
All methods use dynamic binding
questions.explanation: Module 13 - Polymorphism

questions.question: Comparing the two kinds of binding:
options: Dynamic binding is not supported in Java
Static binding makes programs flexible; dynamic binding operates more quickly
Dynamic binding makes programs flexible; static binding operates more quickly
Both are equally fast and flexible
questions.explanation: Module 13 - Polymorphism

questions.question: Dynamic method binding is most useful when you want a method whose parameters:
options: Are always strings, so that the method can print their names
Cannot be objects, because objects are bound at compile time
Might be one of several types, such as any Animal descendant
Are always primitive types, such as int or double values
questions.explanation: Module 13 - Polymorphism

questions.question: When you create an array of objects in Java, you are actually creating:
options: The objects themselves, already constructed
Space for references to objects
A package of objects
A new class
questions.explanation: Module 13 - Polymorphism

questions.question: Animal[] animalRef = new Animal[3]; Given that Animal is abstract, this statement:
options: Reserves memory for three Animal references without instantiating any Animal
Does not compile, because an array cannot be declared using an abstract type
Creates three Animal objects, one for each element of the animalRef array
Creates one Dog, one Cow, and one Snake object to fill the three array elements
questions.explanation: Module 13 - Polymorphism

questions.question: An array of superclass references can hold subclass references:
options: Only if the superclass is abstract, never concrete
Only if the superclass is concrete, never abstract
Never, since every array element must be one type
Whether the superclass is abstract or concrete
questions.explanation: Module 13 - Polymorphism

questions.question: The ability to use the same name for two or more methods in a class is known as:
options: Polymorphism
Static binding
Operation overloading
Encapsulation
questions.explanation: Module 13 - Polymorphism

questions.question: Two methods have the same method signature if:
options: They have the same access specifier and are both declared static in their classes
Their names are the same and the number and type of formal parameters are the same
They are declared in the same package and have the same number of statements inside
Their return types are the same, even if their names and parameters are different
questions.explanation: Module 13 - Polymorphism

questions.question: Given constructors A(), A(int x), A(int x, int y), and A(String x), which is called by new A("hello")?
options: A(String x)
A(int x, int y)
A(int x)
questions.explanation: Module 13 - Polymorphism

questions.question: Declaring two public void a1() {} methods in the same class is:
options: Valid overriding, because the second replaces the first
Valid overloading, because the two methods are separate
Valid only if one of the two methods is declared static
Invalid, reported as a duplicate method declaration
questions.explanation: Module 13 - Polymorphism

questions.question: Can the return type alone distinguish overloaded methods from one another?
options: Only for static methods declared in the same class
Yes, the return type alone always distinguishes them from each other
Only for methods that are declared in an interface
No, the return type does not distinguish overloaded methods
questions.explanation: Module 13 - Polymorphism

questions.question: Declaring methods of the same signature in different, unrelated classes is:
options: Allowed only for constructors
Valid in object-oriented programming
Allowed only if the classes are abstract
Invalid
questions.explanation: Module 13 - Polymorphism

questions.question: For a subclass method to redefine (override) a superclass method:
options: The method signatures of the two methods must be the same
The methods must have different names
The subclass method must have more parameters than the other
The superclass method must be private
questions.explanation: Module 13 - Polymorphism

questions.question: The ability of different objects to perform the appropriate method in response to the same message is known as:
options: Operation overloading
Modularity
Polymorphism
Bundling
questions.explanation: Module 13 - Polymorphism

questions.question: In polymorphism, the sender of a message (such as main()):
options: Must know the exact class of the receiver before it can send any message
Must use a switch statement to choose the method for each type of object
Knows the object can respond, but not its class or how it will respond
Decides which method the receiving object uses to respond to the message
questions.explanation: Module 13 - Polymorphism

questions.question: Polymorphism is facilitated by:
options: Private variables and the use of switch statements to select the correct method
Dynamic binding and the ability to use the same name for similar methods across class definitions
Static binding and the requirement for unique routine names in each and every class definition
Packages and import statements that bring similar classes into the same program
questions.explanation: Module 13 - Polymorphism

questions.question: Polymorphism encourages programmers to specify:
options: Only the data, not the methods
How it should happen rather than what should happen
Only the user interface
What should happen rather than how it should happen
questions.explanation: Module 13 - Polymorphism. This promotes incremental program development.

questions.question: What is polymorphism?
options: The ability of different objects to respond to the same message in their own way
The grouping of related classes and interfaces into one named package
The ability of one class to inherit directly from several parent classes at once
The hiding of an object's internal data and methods from the other objects
questions.explanation: Module 13 - Polymorphism

questions.question: What is static binding?
options: Binding of two classes into one package
Binding of a method call to its code at run time
Binding of data and methods into an object
Binding of a method call to its code at compile time
questions.explanation: Module 13 - Polymorphism

questions.question: What is dynamic binding?
options: Binding of a method call to its code at run time
Binding of a method call to its code at compile time
Binding of a variable to a constant
Binding of attributes to a static class
